The distinction is exact:

> **A model checker searches states inside a fixed representation. An intelligence with a paradigm searches over representations, then uses model checking inside the most promising compressed regions.**

A conventional model checker receives:

\[
(M,\ P,\ H)
\]

A model, property and horizon are already defined. It asks whether \(M\models_H P\).

The Kuhn Engine must choose or revise:

\[
S=
(\phi,\ Z,\ \widehat T,\ O,\ P,\ \Pi,\ \mathcal U)
\]

Where:

- \(\phi\): projection from raw events into abstract states
- \(Z\): ontology and state variables
- \(\widehat T\): compressed transition model
- \(O\): observations considered relevant
- \(P\): properties and prospective commitments
- \(\Pi\): available action policy
- \(\mathcal U\): uncertainty and residual-err
